statement.p: A person walking along a straight path has her velocity in miles per hour at time t given by the function v(t) = 0.25t^3 - 1.5t^2 + 3t + 0.25, for times in the interval 0 \leq t \leq 2. This function is positive and increasing in that interval. The graph of this function is also given in each of the three diagrams below.

image.shortdescription: Diagram A: a graph of a function v with four rectangles whose top-left corners intersect v.

description.p: The graph of v(t) on 0\leq t\leq 2. There are four rectangles of width 0.5 standing side-by-side on the t-axis. The rectangles are labeled A_1 through A_4 from left to right, and each hits the graph at their top-left corners. Because v is increasing, there is a lot of empty space under the graph and above the tops of the rectangles.

image.shortdescription: Diagram B: a graph of a function v with four rectangles whose top-right corners intersect v.

description.p: The same graph of v(t) with four rectangles arranged as before, but with different labels and heights. The rectangles are labeled B_1 through B_4 and each hits the graph at their top-right corners. Because v is increasing, the top-left corners of each rectangle extend above the graph.

image.shortdescription: Diagram C: a graph of a function v with four rectangles whose top-centers intersect v.

description.p: The same graph of v(t) with four rectangles arranged as before, but with different labels and heights. The rectangles are labeled C_1 through C_4 and each hits the graph at the center of their top edge. Because v is increasing, there is a little bit of space below the graph and above the rectangles to the right of center while little bit of each rectangle extends above the graph left of center.

statement.p: Note that in each diagram, we use four rectangles to estimate the area under y = v(t) on the interval [0, 2], but the method by which the four rectangles' respective heights are decided varies among the three individual graphs.

Think about how the heights of the rectangles in Diagram A are being chosen. Determine the value of S=A_1+A_2+A_3+A_4 by evaluating the function y=v(t) at appropriately-chosen values and observing the width of each rectangle. Note, for example, that A_3 = v(1)\cdot \frac{1}{2} = 2\cdot \frac{1}{2} = 1.
Use the rectangles in Diagram B to find the value of T=B_1+B_2+B_3+B_4.
Use the rectangles in Diagram C to find the value of U=C_1+C_2+C_3+C_4.
Which estimate do you think is the best approximation of D, the total distance the person traveled on [0,2]?

li.p: Rectangles are always below the graph of v(t)
Rectangles are always above the graph of v(t)
Rectangles are partially above the graph of v(t) and partially below
